title: The Town That Literally Danced Itself To Death
sources: John Waller (2008), 'A Time to Dance, a Time to Die: The Extraordinary Story of the Dancing Plague of 1518'
The Lancet (2009), 'A forgotten plague: making sense of dancing mania'

lines.text: In 1518, an entire city caught a sickness that made them dance until they collapsed.
lines.caps: In 1518, | an entire city | caught a sickness | that made them dance.

lines.text: It started when one woman stepped into the street and began dancing uncontrollably.
Within thirty days, over four hundred citizens joined her, dancing frantically day and night.
Terrified local doctors concluded that the only cure was... even more dancing!
So the city council built wooden stages, hired professional musicians, and ordered them to play non-stop.
This backfired completely, causing hundreds more people to join the feverish dance party!
Dancers had bloody feet and pure exhaustion, yet their bodies kept moving for weeks,
before the mysterious trance suddenly vanished as strangely as it began,
leaving historians still baffled five hundred years later!
